FIRMWARE.because: The extension lives in the xv6 kernel and its user-space stub: the proof configures no boot-time machine state and depends on none. xv6 installs its own trap handling, so there is no firmware layer beneath the claim whose configuration could change the outcome.

KERNEL.because: This card implements a kernel subsystem and verifies it: a new getscount syscall threaded from the user-space stub through xv6's single dispatch funnel into per-process uint64 counter tables, with a compile-time check on the dispatch table size and fork-lifecycle isolation in the tests. The verified claim depends on kernel behavior because the claim is kernel behavior: each invocation increments the calling process's counter and no other's.

ALGORITHM.because: The mechanism is shaped by xv6's internals: its syscall numbering, its process table layout, its single dispatch funnel. title: medeleg bit 12 routes the instruction page fault to S-mode
summary: A bare-metal RISC-V program builds a minimal Sv39 table with one invalid leaf and issues the same S-mode jump to the unmapped page in two phases. With medeleg bit 12 clear, the fetch traps in M-mode with mcause 0xc and mepc at the fault page; with the bit set, it traps in S-mode with scause 0xc, sepc and stval both at the fault page. A quiet window with all interrupt enables clear leaves both trap counts unchanged.

ISA.because: Matters at ISA because medeleg is the privileged machine contract for trap delegation: bit 12 selects the destination for instruction page faults, and the test log shows the same S-mode jump to an unmapped page arriving in M-mode with mcause 0xc when the bit is clear and in S-mode with scause 0xc, sepc and stval at the fault page, when the bit is set.

MICROARCH.because: Not at MICROARCH because the test log asserts trap destinations, cause codes, and exact trap pcs across 3 byte-identical runs, never timing. Moving cache or pipeline behavior changes when the fetch faults, never whether medeleg bit 12 selects M-mode or S-mode, and the 32 checks assert only the routing.

FIRMWARE.because: Matters at FIRMWARE because trap delegation is configured by M-mode boot firmware: the test log is exactly that firmware-level act, writing medeleg bit 12, dropping to S-mode, and executing the faulting jump, so the claim leans on boot-time machine-mode configuration.

KERNEL.because: Not at KERNEL because no kernel subsystem takes part in the claim: the S-mode handler is a test stub recording scause, sepc, and stval, not a scheduler or memory manager, and the routing verdict holds identically under any kernel.

ALGORITHM.because: Not at ALGORITHM because selecting a trap destination through a delegation CSR is a hardware register contract stated in RISC-V privileged terms (medeleg, mcause, scause). It cannot be restated as an ISA-independent computation, so it fails the identical-on-every-ISA test.

title: inexact fadd.d sets fflags.NX alone; exact fadd.d sets nothing
summary: An M-mode program clears fcsr, executes one inexact double-precision add, and reads back the accrued flags. The inexact fadd.d of 1e16 and 1.0 rounds under RNE and sets only the NX flag; the exact control fadd.d of 1.0 and 2.0 sets no flag at all. The fcsr is restored to its boot value and the trap count stays zero.

ISA.because: Matters at ISA because the F extension defines fcsr and its accrued exception flags: the test log shows one inexact fadd.d setting exactly the NX bit with NV, DZ, OF, and UF clear, and one exact fadd.d leaving fcsr at zero, which is the machine contract for inexact flag accrual in action.

MICROARCH.because: Not at MICROARCH because the test log asserts only flag bits and result words across 3 byte-identical runs, never timing. A different pipeline or FPU implementation changes how fast the add completes, never which accrued flag the inexact result sets, and the 18 checks assert only the flag outcomes.

FIRMWARE.because: Matters at FIRMWARE because the floating-point unit is enabled by M-mode software: the test log enables FS in mstatus, asserts no interrupt can fire, and installs a counting trap handler as a safety net, so the claim leans on machine-mode configuration of the execution environment.

KERNEL.because: Not at KERNEL because the module runs bare metal with no operating system loaded: the trap handler is a counting safety net that never fires, not a scheduler or driver, and the flag verdict holds identically under any kernel.

ALGORITHM.because: Not at ALGORITHM because which accrued flag an inexact operation sets is a hardware CSR contract, not a portable computation. The RNE rounding analysis is mathematics, but the verified claim, that this hart sets NX and nothing else, is stated in RISC-V terms and fails the identical-on-every-ISA test.
